methods.name: Peer-Median

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
WeaveGrid is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Apoorv Bhargava and John Taggart, having raised $78M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company peers in the climate and energy sector, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $78M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $148M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median valuation across this set is $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

The two methods produce a triangulated valuation range of $126M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $574M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in peer selection and stage-adjustment methodology. The peer-median method yields substantially higher values, driven by later-stage comparable valuations; stage-progression is more conservative. Key uncertainties include whether later-stage Series C comparables appropriately anchor a Series B valuation, capital efficiency relative to peers, and the specific technology risk profile of WeaveGrid relative to the broader cohort.
